To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extent of benzo(α)pyrene metabolism in the lung of man varies considerably among individuals, and that the extent of metabolism of benzo( α)pyrene and that of ethoxyresoruf in the same individuals are closely correlated.

human lung microsomes are able to metabolize benzo(a) pyrene to a large extent, that the extent of benzo (a) pyrene metabolism varies 13 fold among individuals, and that the 7, 8 dihydrodiol is the major metabolite.

the extent and type of benzo(a)-pyrene metabolism in human lung microsomes prepared from surgical specimens is highly variable among individuals and that, in most cases, the extent of hydroxylation exceeds that of dihydrodiol formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of an analytical technique for the simultaneous measurement of the major metabolites of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon benzo(a) pyrene in biological samples.
the biotransformation and mutagenic activation of benzo(a)-pyrene in human lung microsomes.
the metabolism of benzo(a)-pyrene in microsomal fractions from surgically removed human lung tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human lung microsomes are able to metabolize benzo(a) pyrene to a limited extent and that the extent of metabolism varies considerably from person to person.
the metabolism of benzo(a)-pyrene by human lungs is qualitatively similar to that by laboratory animals, but that the extent varies considerably between individuals.
the lung microsomal fraction prepared from surgical specimens is a useful tool for the assessment of human lung microsomes in benzo(a) pyrene metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human lung contains a cytochrome P-450 system that is qualitatively and quantitatively different from those of rodents and that the human lung is a site for oxidative biotransformation.
the metabolism of benzo(a)-pyrene in the lung is qualitatively normal and in many individuals quantitatively normal.
the extent and the pattern of benzo(a)-pyrene metabolism are highly variable among individuals.
